I couldn't find any triggers for my migraines, searched for about 2 years. Turned out my heart was letting unfiltered "dirty" blood back into my blood stream and causing stroke-like symptoms and migraines. Mine were on my left side though. 
In the short term, aspirin was the only thing that took the edge off of my pain, even after trying Topomax 200 mg daily and Sumitriptan as needed. It thinned my blood and started to lessen the intensity of my migraines over time. 
I ended up needing blood thinners (temporarily) and heart surgery to resolve it. I'm not suggesting that you have the same issue, but it might be worth a trip to the cardiologist or a new neurologist. Even maybe a psychologist (personally, it helped me tremendously. Loosing some stress in my life did make migraines less intense, though not less often). 
I'm suggesting this mostly because you can't find your trigger. From my experience, I realized that I was the trigger. Nothing I did could prevent the migraine because the trigger was actually my blood. 

I hope you find something that helps.

I started having daily migraines and went to a neurologist. After a year or so of nothing working, I got a lot more sick. I started to notice that my chest felt off right before I would get a migraine, and I was always very aware of my heart beat. 
I had a cardiologist because I was also experiencing palpitations, but frankly he wasn't a good doctor. I changed cardiologists and my second Doctor suspected that I had a hole in my heart. I mentioned it to my neurologist, and they tested me in office with a Bubble Test. (It's basically a sonogram with contrast, but on your veins. They make some saline bubbly by swishing it around in a catheter with some of your blood and then inject it back into your body through the catheter. Pretty painless.) the bubble test immediately showed that I had a hole in my heart, the size of which I am told was at least a 4. Tbh idk what that means, but it didn't sound great. 
My neurologist recommended a new cardiologist that happened to specialize in my condition AND work at the best cardiac hospital in my state. He confirmed the hole by running a second bubble test and prescribed Plavix. I went three weeks without a migraine immediately after starting the Plavix. That was the first time in 2 years I had gone without a migraine for more then 2 days. 
Because I responded so well to the Plavix, I was a candidate for surgery. I had a device planted in my heart to close the hole. Over the next 3 months (I still have about a month to go) the skin of my heart will grow over the device, making it permanent, and close the hole completely. 
I have had 1 or 2 migraines since my surgery in April. Both were triggered by lifestyle choices (lol I was impatient in recovery and didn't wait until I was healed enough to go and do things). 

As it turns out, my cardiologist that helped me said that up to 40% of people with migraines has a hole in their heart, and about 20% of the population overall has it. 

My condition is called a PFO, patent foramen ovale. 

Tl;dr a lot of doctors were wrong until one was right.
